display.text:
# Context Pack: `run-cli-observation` — Run observation and cancellation CLI

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: operator-interfaces. Risk: normal. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

The `ultraplan run` subcommands are the operator's window onto the durable run-control store (`.ultraplan/run-control.db`, owned by `internal/runcontrol`). Five doors: `list` (newest-first filtered page with opaque keyset cursor), `show` (one validated snapshot), `follow` (replay committed events from a decimal sequence, then poll until the run reaches terminal state), `cancel` (reason-whitelisted durable cancellation request), and `diagnostics` (repository health projection plus an optional bounded, payload-free support export). All five are local-only: they never contact a provider (docs/cli-reference.md:492-504). The same repository capability is re-exported as `RunUseCases` for the web and TUI surfaces, making this package the shared read/cancel vocabulary for durable runs. Observation never mutates a run's lifecycle; interruption of `follow` stops observation only (run_commands.go:188-193; user-guide.md:388-391).

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Dispatch and repository acquisition
`app.Run` (app.go:88-178) dispatches `run` at app.go:161-162 to `runRun(deps, args[1:])`. `runRun` (run_commands.go:19-40) admits `--help/-h` (prints help without opening any store — test-enforced) and routes to the five handlers; unknown subcommand → ExitUsage. Every handler first calls `runRepository` (run_commands.go:42-59): workspace discovery (`--workspace` flag validated against the `ultraplan.yml` marker, else `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, else cwd upward walk; discovery.go:21-61) → ExitWorkspace class on failure; `deps.runControl == nil` → ExitRuntime "run-control.init"; `loadEffectiveConfig` → ExitConfig class; then `deps.runControl.repository(ctx, root.Path, runControlRetentionPolicy(effective.Config))` → ExitRuntime "run-control.open" on failure.

`runControlState.repository` (run_control.go:37-75) is a mutex-guarded per-workspace process singleton: one `*runcontrol.SQLiteRepository` plus one `LocalFileLogger`, retained for process lifetime and closed by `defer runControl.Close()` in `app.Run` (app.go:108-109). Opening performs, in order: `OpenSQLite` (creates `.ultraplan/` 0700 + `run-control.db` 0600 if absent, verifies WAL/FULL/FK/busy pragmas, migrates schema, enforces private modes; sqlite.go:60-134,154-227), logger open + `SetLogger`, then **startup `Reconcile(NativeProcessProbe{}, ReconcileOptions{})`** — so every command, including pure reads, may write (mark owners stalled, terminalize abandoned/expired-lease runs, append reconciliation_log rows). Startup reconcile failure closes both handles and aborts the command ("startup run reconciliation failed", run_control.go:66-70). A second call with a different retention policy errors deterministically ("retention policy changed during the process lifetime", run_control.go:47-49).

`runControlRetentionPolicy` (run_control.go:153-157) converts config strings with `time.ParseDuration`, ignoring parse errors (zero durations later fall back to defaults in `normalizeRetentionPolicy`, retention.go:13-33); quota bytes pass through.

### 2.2 `run list` (run_commands.go:61-103)
Flags: `--json`, `--project`, `--sprint`, `--study`, `--lifecycle` (comma-separated), `--limit` (default 50; help advertises 1..200), `--after <opaque cursor>`. Help is checked before parsing; parse errors or leftover positional args → ExitUsage via `firstFlagError`. `parseLifecycleFilter` (379-392) trims/splits and validates each token against `Lifecycle.IsValid()` (11 valid states, model.go:18-41); unknown token → ExitUsage.

`Repository.List` (lifecycle.go:196-266): limit 0→50, bounds 1..200 else `invalidField`; filters are equality predicates on `project_id`/`sprint_id`/`study_id` plus `lifecycle IN (...)`; ordering is `updated_at DESC, run_id DESC`; `After` decodes an opaque cursor (base64url JSON `{updated_at RFC3339Nano, run_id}`, ≤1024 decoded bytes, timestamp+RunID validated; lifecycle.go:268-291) into a strict keyset predicate `(updated_at < ? OR (updated_at = ? AND run_id < ?))`; fetches limit+1 rows and, when more exist, sets `NextCursor` from the last *included* row before trimming. Each listed run is then loaded through `Snapshot` (N reads), each individually passed through `Snapshot.Validate()` (model.go:333-366). Text output prints `%s  %-20s %-18s %s` (RunID, lifecycle, liveness, slash-joined target via `formatRunTarget` 427-435), "No durable runs found." when empty, and `Next cursor: …` when paginated. JSON output uses the shared envelope (`writeJSON`, json_output.go:20-31: schema_version 1, command, workspace path, status "ok", generated_at, result = Page).

### 2.3 `run show <run-id>` (105-129)
One positional run ID (flags reordered ahead of positionals by `orderRunArgs`, 463-481); `Snapshot(ctx, RunID(arg))` validates the opaque-ID shape first (`run_` + 26 lowercase base32 chars, id.go:65-89) → invalid shape becomes ErrInvalidArgument; missing row becomes ErrNotFound ("run is not retained"). Text rendering `renderRunSnapshot` (416-425): Run / Target / Lifecycle / Liveness / Product status (falls back to literal "unknown") / Cancellation state / Accepted / Updated (RFC3339) / Last sequence / Oldest retained sequence / History complete / Record state, plus `Terminal: outcome (reason)` when present. `--json` wraps the raw snapshot in the envelope with status "ok".

### 2.4 `run follow <run-id>` (131-195)
Flags: `--json` (newline-delimited events), `--after <decimal sequence>` default "0" (ParseUint base 10, 64-bit; non-decimal → ExitUsage). A pre-loop `Snapshot` call validates existence before streaming. Loop body: `Events(ctx, runID, after, 512)` (sqlite.go:809-854 — strictly increasing sequences `> after`, batch cap 512, payloads decoded from stored JSON); text mode prints `seq  type(padded) stage omitted=N` (payload fields are not printed); JSON mode encodes the full persisted Event struct including its sanitized Payload map. Then a fresh `Snapshot`: loop returns nil only when `Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence`. Otherwise it waits — 250 ms after a full 512-batch or while `after < LastSequence` (catch-up), else 1 s idle — and exits cleanly on `deps.ctx.Done()` with the comment "Observation cancellation never changes the durable run". The timer starts pre-stopped (`NewTimer(0)` + drain). Polling only: the repository Notifier hook is nil in this composition.

### 2.5 `run cancel <run-id>` (197-228)
Flags: `--json`, `--reason` default "user_requested". `canonicalCancellationReason` (394-401) whitelists exactly: `user_requested`, `operator_requested`, `shutdown_requested`, `quota_exceeded`; anything else → ExitUsage. `RequestCancellation` (lifecycle.go:70-134) trims/bounds-checks the reason, opens an immediate transaction, reloads the snapshot, and: if terminal OR cancellation state ≠ none → commits the read and returns `(current, changed=false, nil)` (idempotent no-op); otherwise appends a `cancellation` event (payload `{state: requested, reason}`) and CAS-updates `runs SET lifecycle='cancelling', cancellation_state='requested' … WHERE terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state='none' AND last_sequence = ?`; lost race → typed CodeConflict (retryable flag set). CLI text output: `Run: %s / Cancellation: %s / Changed: %t`; JSON output embeds `{changed, run: snapshot}`. Note the request is recorded regardless of owner liveness — delivery to the running owner happens owner-side (control loops acknowledge within their tick; outer-inner-double-fencing seam).

### 2.6 `run diagnostics` (230-276)
Flags: `--json`, `--support-export <path>`. `Repository.Health` (sqlite.go:856-914) reads journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys pragmas, counts active runs (accepted/queued/running/cancelling), stalled runs (non-terminal + liveness stalled), cancellation-uncertain rows, reconciliation backlog (unclaimed past grace or expired lease past `ReconciliationGrace`=45 s, joined to attempts), oldest backlog age (min of accepted_at vs lease_expires_at over the backlog), storage bytes (all regular files prefixed `run-control.db` — db/WAL/SHM), soft/hard quotas (soft = hard − 16 MiB reserved headroom), and process-local `LocalMetrics` counters (metrics.go:17-25). Status escalates ok → degraded (≥ soft quota) → failed (≥ hard quota) with appended diagnostic strings. Text output prints nine labeled lines plus `Support export:` when written. `--json` wraps `{health, support_export?}` with the envelope **status field set to `string(health.Status)`** (ok/degraded/failed) rather than the constant "ok" used by the other four subcommands.

Support export (`writeRunSupportExport`, 306-377): unfiltered `List(limit 50)`; config trio (full_history, tombstone_history, workspace_quota_bytes) with source classes from `effective.Sources`; `ReconciliationEvidence(ctx, 100)` behind an anonymous-interface assertion (newest-first, evidence reduced to allowlisted classification strings, lifecycle.go:532-572); `ReadLocalLogs(root, 100)` (local_log.go:113-155 — rejects symlink/oversize/non-regular log files, skips malformed lines, keeps newest N via sliding window); per run, the first 50 events from sequence 0 reduced to `{sequence, type, omission}` — **event payloads are excluded**. The whole document is marshaled indented, rejected if > 1 MiB, then written `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY` mode 0600 (existing file → error), fsynced, closed, with deferred remove-on-failure. When `--support-export` is set, diagnostics re-runs workspace discovery and config load (251-258) even though `runRepository` already performed both.

### 2.7 `RunUseCases` adapter (run_usecases.go)
Type aliases for all runcontrol DTOs plus sentinel error aliases (invalid-argument/not-found/conflict/unsupported-schema). `RunUseCases` (Runs/Run/RunEvents/CancelRun/RunHealth) is documented as "the surface-neutral durable observation and command boundary. Its DTOs contain only sanitized facts owned by run control"; `repositoryRunUseCases` delegates 1:1 to the Repository. Consumers: web composition (serve_commands.go:80), TUI (`useCases.runs`, tui_commands.go:51), dashboard runs page (sprint_commands.go:407). This adapter is the seam face consumed by web-operation-hub-sse and tui-console.

### 2.8 Write-path context inside the assigned files (run_control.go)
`run_control.go` also hosts the durable write spine used by runtime-backed commands: `controlledRuntime.StartRun` (159-343) Accept→Claim→fence, persists sanitized event drafts through `OnEvent` with content-aware progress coalescing (250 ms window keyed type/stage/task/payload-hash, omission accounting merged into the next commit), a 1 s control goroutine (snapshot poll; requested cancellation ⇒ AcknowledgeCancellation + cancel; Heartbeat every 5 s under a 15 s lease; Reconcile every 10 s), persistence-failure handling that proposes `persistence_degraded` under a 30 s background context, and `terminalOutcome` mapping (deadline→timed_out, cancel→cancelled, err/failed-status→failed, else succeeded). Its sanitization pipeline feeds the journal this surface observes: `runtimeEventDraft` (417-545) maps runtime kinds to event types, drops sensitive keys (`isSensitivePayloadKey` markers secret/token/password/authorization/cookie/api_key/apikey/credential/auth), bounds keys (≤128, no control chars) and values (`boundedPayloadValue`, 32 KiB), flattens one level of nesting with a promote-list (tool/title/detail/text/delta/content/message/action/state/status/native_type/line, ≤30 entries), captures tool identity/arguments/result/error with depth-5 alias search and `redactObservableValue` string-marker redaction ([REDACTED] for bearer /sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/private-key), and records omissions for raw-present/raw-omitted/truncated shapes. A second gate applies at storage: `sanitizeEventDraft` (sanitize.go:26-61) enforces the ~35-field allowlist (sanitize.go:10-21), adds sensitive fragments prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command (80-88), rejects absolute paths/Windows-drive strings/credential markers/control chars (90-104), replaces oversize allowed detail with a warning event, and caps encoded size at 128 KiB. The write spine itself belongs primarily to durable-operation-spine/run-journal-fencing; it is described here because the file sits inside this surface's assigned paths ... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

## 3. Inputs / outputs

Inputs: argv (subcommand, flags, run-ID positional); workspace discovery sources (`--workspace`, `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, cwd marker walk); effective config incl. env overrides `ULTRAPLAN_RUN_CONTROL_FULL_HISTORY/TOMBSTONE_HISTORY/WORKSPACE_QUOTA_BYTES` (config.go:140-142) validated ≥1h/≥24h/≥64 MiB with tombstone ≥ full (config.go:487-500); `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`) and `.ultraplan/run-control.log`; wall clock; signal context (SIGINT/SIGTERM via `signal.NotifyContext`, main.go:15-17) which reaches `follow`'s wait select and repository calls as ctx cancellation.

Outputs: stdout human tables/lines or JSON envelopes (schema_version 1); one-line stderr errors carrying exit classes; support export file (private 0600, ≤1 MiB, O_EXCL); process exit codes from the reachable set {0, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 workspace, 5 validation/not-found, 6 runtime/store, 8 partial conflict/terminal} (app.go:15-25; mapRunControlError 403-414: ErrInvalidArgument→2, ErrNotFound→5, ErrConflict/ErrTerminal→8, everything else incl. Busy/Unavailable/Corrupt/Permission/Quota/Invariant/UnsupportedSchema→6). Side outputs common to all five doors because of pool startup: DB/WAL creation, chmod enforcement, log appends, reconcile writes (§2.1).

## 4. Authoritative state

The authoritative durable state is entirely in `internal/runcontrol`'s SQLite store: `runs` (snapshot columns incl. lifecycle/liveness/record_state/last_sequence/oldest_retained_sequence/history_complete/omission_total/cancellation_*/terminal_*), `attempts` (fencing generations, leases, heartbeats, process birth identity), `events` (immutable — BEFORE UPDATE trigger raises; PK (run_id, sequence)), `operation_aliases`, `reconciliation_log` (evidence bounded to 16 KiB JSON, classification-only exposure on read) (schema sqlite.go:229-342). Durability posture: WAL, synchronous=FULL, foreign_keys=on, busy_timeout 5 s, immediate transactions, pragma verification at open (207-227). This surface owns no new durable state — it projects and (via cancel/reconcile) mutates through the repository. Process-local state: the `runControlState` pool (repo+logger+policy per workspace) and per-process metrics counters (not aggregate across processes). Retention/compaction (full 168h default → compacted → tombstone 720h → delete; per-run caps 4096 events / 16 MiB advancing `oldest_retained_sequence`, retention.go:58-160) reshape what observation can replay; snapshots remain truthful with explicit replay boundaries. The support export is a derived artifact, never authoritative.

## 5. Invariants (as implemented)

- Every command, read or write, opens the same per-process repository handle and runs startup Reconcile before serving; retention policy must be stable per process (run_control.go:37-75).
- Every returned snapshot is validated on read (`Snapshot.Validate` enforces lifecycle/terminal/liveness coherence, timestamps monotonic from acceptance, replay-boundary arithmetic model.go:349-364); corrupt rows fail the whole command rather than render partially.
- List order is deterministic (updated_at DESC, run_id DESC) and pagination is keyset-based; cursors are opaque, bounded (≤1024 decoded bytes), and fully validated (timestamp + canonical RunID).
- Follow delivers strictly increasing sequences > `--after` in batches ≤512, terminates only on terminal-lifecycle-and-drained, and treats SIGINT/SIGTERM as end-of-observation only.
- Cancel requests are idempotent at the store (second request returns changed=false), CAS-arbitrated against concurrent state change, and can never overwrite a won terminal.
- Journal content displayed was gated twice before persistence (app-layer redaction/bounding §2.8 + storage allowlist sanitize.go); text modes print no payload fields at all; support export excludes payloads and asserts exclusion of absolute workspace paths in tests.
- Bounded resources everywhere: list pages ≤200; event batches ≤512; export ≤1 MiB, ≤50 runs × 50 event headers, ≤100 evidence rows, ≤100 log records; local log ≤1 MiB total, ≤4 KiB/line, drop-on-overflow; payload values ≤32 KiB; encoded events ≤128 KiB; per-run journals compacted at 4096 events/16 MiB.
- Private-file discipline: `.ultraplan` 0700, db/log/export 0600, symlink rejection for dir/db/log, chmod verify after set (sqlite.go:154-205; local_log.go:43-65; export O_EXCL).
- Help paths never touch the repository or create files (test-enforced, run_commands_test.go:83-92).
- Stable exit-class mapping for every repository error family (mapRunControlError).

## 6. Trust boundaries

- Operator-supplied run IDs must match the strict opaque base32 grammar before any SQL executes (id.go:73-89); cursors are decoded, size-capped, and semantically validated before use; all SQL is parameterized.
- Trust boundary named in the assignment: **journal payload projection passes sanitizer/redaction before display**. Runtime payloads never reach stdout verbatim: they pass the app-layer redactor/bounder (isSensitivePayloadKey, redactObservableValue, boundedPayloadValue) and then the storage allowlist gate (sanitizeEventDraft); what `follow --json` emits is the persisted, already-sanitized payload map; text modes emit only sequence/type/stage/omission-count; the support export strips payloads entirely.
- Sensitive-content controls operate by deny-marker matching at two layers (secret/token/password/auth*/cookie/api_key/credential…; plus prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command and absolute-path/Windows-drive rejection at storage) rather than positive encoding; `[REDACTED]` substitution applies to tool argument/result trees.
- Local trust model: POSIX permissions are the only access control; any local process/user that can reach `.ultraplan/` can read the store and request cancellations. No auth, session, or origin machinery exists at this door.
- The support export is written to an operator-chosen path with O_EXCL (refuses overwrite) and 0600; its contents include sanitized log records and classification-only reconciliation evidence.
- Config-sourced retention/quota values cross from yml/env into store-opening policy; source classes (default/workspace/env) are recorded into exports for provenance.

## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics

External effects per invocation: possible creation/chmod of `.ultraplan/{run-control.db,-wal,-shm,run-control.log}`; startup Reconcile writes (stalled marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals for expired/unclaimed owners past 45 s grace, reconciliation_log inserts); log appends; `cancel` appends a cancellation event and flips lifecycle to cancelling under CAS; `diagnostics --support-export` creates one new file (never overwrites); stdout/stderr/exit-code emission. Retry semantics: the observation surface itself does not retry — typed retryable flags exist on store errors (Busy/Unavailable) but only write-spine callers loop (appendRunEventWithRetry 5 s deadline, proposeRunTerminalWithRetry 250 ms windows, run_control.go:345-368). Cancellation lanes: this door only records the request; acknowledgement/delivery lives in owner control loops; a request can lose the immutable terminal race to an earlier completion (user-guide.md:384-386 documents this to operators). Restart/recovery: each fresh process re-reconciles on first command; reconcile decisions use exact process-birth identity probing and never infer success from artifact presence or PID existence alone (lifecycle.go:481-495). ## 10. Tests (evidence map)

Baseline green: internal/app 57.8% statements, internal/runcontrol 68.7% (review/baseline/go-test-cover.txt:2,12).

## 11. Explicit unknowns / open questions (for later reviewers)

1. Follow exposes no replay-gap signal: events below `oldest_retained_sequence` are simply absent from the stream, while TRD.md:1255 requires typed retention-gap results "rather than silently beginning a partial stream" and the web door implements `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` (run_handlers.go:968-979). Whether the CLI's silent-empty behavior satisfies the contract for operators is unresolved in-tree; likewise `--after` beyond `LastSequence` on a non-terminal run polls at 1 Hz indefinitely without feedback.
2. Read commands mutate durable state via startup Reconcile (stall marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals, evidence rows). The architecture intends reconciliation-at-open, but operator-facing docs describe list/show/follow purely as inspection; the observable consequence (opening a laptop after a crash rewrites other runs' liveness/terminals as a side effect of a "read") is undocumented in-tree.
3. Envelope status divergence: `run diagnostics --json` sets envelope status to health.Status (ok/degraded/failed) while the other four subcommands hard-code "ok"; run JSON surfaces are absent from the compatibility-sensitive stable-JSON list (cli-reference.md:474-491), so consumer expectations are unpinned.
4. `runControlRetentionPolicy` ignores `time.ParseDuration` errors (run_control.go:154-156); config.Load validation should catch malformed yml/env upstream, but the swallow-pattern's interaction with normalizeRetentionPolicy defaults is unannotated.
5. Support export truncation is silent: first 50 events per run, ≤50 runs, ≤100 logs/evidence rows — no marker records that deeper history exists; size check measures marshaled bytes before the appended newline (off-by-one immaterial but unspecified).
6. `runDiagnostics` repeats discoverWorkspace + loadEffectiveConfig inside the support branch although runRepository already performed both (251-258 vs 242-245); intent unstated.
7. Cancellation authorization: any local process able to open the workspace can request cancellation with any whitelisted reason regardless of ownership; how TRD.md:2206's "mutation still requires fresh authorization and a resolvable current owner" maps onto the CLI-local trust model is undefined in-tree.
8. List loads one Snapshot per row outside a shared transaction; a page can mix vintages when runs update mid-listing, and cost scales linearly with limit. Consistency expectations are nowhere stated.
9. `Query.TargetKind` filtering exists in the store but no CLI flag exposes it; reachability limited to web/TUI/in-process callers — asymmetry unexplained.
10. `Health.Metrics` are per-process atomic counters embedded in JSON and exports; meaning under multiple simultaneous CLI/server processes (each sees only its own counts) is undefined for consumers.
11. `orderRunArgs` hand-rolls flag/positional reordering per subcommand with a fixed recognized-flag table (--json/--help plus valued flags); edge-case equivalence with stdlib parsing (e.g. `--limit=x`, repeated positionals, `--` terminator) is untested.
12. Platform assumptions inherited unconditionally: chmod-mode verification, symlink Lstat checks, native process-birth probing with a stub for unsupported platforms (process_other.go); behavior of enforcePrivateMode/probe on non-POSIX systems is defined only by those stubs.

— End of context pack. Descriptive only; no defect claims made or implied.

## 1. Purpose

The `ultraplan run` subcommands are the operator's window onto the durable run-control store (`.ultraplan/run-control.db`, owned by `internal/runcontrol`). Five doors: `list` (newest-first filtered page with opaque keyset cursor), `show` (one validated snapshot), `follow` (replay committed events from a decimal sequence, then poll until the run reaches terminal state), `cancel` (reason-whitelisted durable cancellation request), and `diagnostics` (repository health projection plus an optional bounded, payload-free support export). All five are local-only: they never contact a provider (docs/cli-reference.md:492-504). The same repository capability is re-exported as `RunUseCases` for the web and TUI surfaces, making this package the shared read/cancel vocabulary for durable runs. Observation never mutates a run's lifecycle; interruption of `follow` stops observation only (run_commands.go:188-193; user-guide.md:388-391).

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Dispatch and repository acquisition
`app.Run` (app.go:88-178) dispatches `run` at app.go:161-162 to `runRun(deps, args[1:])`. `runRun` (run_commands.go:19-40) admits `--help/-h` (prints help without opening any store — test-enforced) and routes to the five handlers; unknown subcommand → ExitUsage. Every handler first calls `runRepository` (run_commands.go:42-59): workspace discovery (`--workspace` flag validated against the `ultraplan.yml` marker, else `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, else cwd upward walk; discovery.go:21-61) → ExitWorkspace class on failure; `deps.runControl == nil` → ExitRuntime "run-control.init"; `loadEffectiveConfig` → ExitConfig class; then `deps.runControl.repository(ctx, root.Path, runControlRetentionPolicy(effective.Config))` → ExitRuntime "run-control.open" on failure.

`runControlState.repository` (run_control.go:37-75) is a mutex-guarded per-workspace process singleton: one `*runcontrol.SQLiteRepository` plus one `LocalFileLogger`, retained for process lifetime and closed by `defer runControl.Close()` in `app.Run` (app.go:108-109). Opening performs, in order: `OpenSQLite` (creates `.ultraplan/` 0700 + `run-control.db` 0600 if absent, verifies WAL/FULL/FK/busy pragmas, migrates schema, enforces private modes; sqlite.go:60-134,154-227), logger open + `SetLogger`, then **startup `Reconcile(NativeProcessProbe{}, ReconcileOptions{})`** — so every command, including pure reads, may write (mark owners stalled, terminalize abandoned/expired-lease runs, append reconciliation_log rows). Startup reconcile failure closes both handles and aborts the command ("startup run reconciliation failed", run_control.go:66-70). A second call with a different retention policy errors deterministically ("retention policy changed during the process lifetime", run_control.go:47-49).

`runControlRetentionPolicy` (run_control.go:153-157) converts config strings with `time.ParseDuration`, ignoring parse errors (zero durations later fall back to defaults in `normalizeRetentionPolicy`, retention.go:13-33); quota bytes pass through.

53: The authoritative durable state is entirely in `internal/runcontrol`'s SQLite store: `runs` (snapshot columns incl. lifecycle/liveness/record_state/last_sequence/oldest_retained_sequence/history_complete/omission_total/cancellation_*/terminal_*), `attempts` (fencing generations, leases, heartbeats, process birth identity), `events` (immutable — BEFORE UPDATE trigger raises; PK (run_id, sequence)), `operation_aliases`, `reconciliation_log` (evidence bounded to 16 KiB JSON, classification-only exposure on read) (schema sqlite.go:229-342). Durability posture: WAL, synchronous=FULL, foreign_keys=on, busy_timeout 5 s, immediate transactions, pragma verification at open (207-227). This surface owns no new durable state — it projects and (via cancel/reconcile) mutates through the repository. Process-local state: the `runControlState` pool (repo+logger+policy per workspace) and per-process metrics counters (not aggregate across processes). Retention/compaction (full 168h default → compacted → tombstone 720h → delete; per-run caps 4096 events / 16 MiB advancing `oldest_retained_sequence`, retention.go:58-160) reshape what observation can replay; snapshots remain truthful with explicit replay boundaries. The support export is a derived artifact, never authoritative.
54: 
55: ## 5. Invariants (as implemented)
56: 
57: - Every command, read or write, opens the same per-process repository handle and runs startup Reconcile before serving; retention policy must be stable per process (run_control.go:37-75).
58: - Every returned snapshot is validated on read (`Snapshot.Validate` enforces lifecycle/terminal/liveness coherence, timestamps monotonic from acceptance, replay-boundary arithmetic model.go:349-364); corrupt rows fail the whole command rather than render partially.
59: - List order is deterministic (updated_at DESC, run_id DESC) and pagination is keyset-based; cursors are opaque, bounded (≤1024 decoded bytes), and fully validated (timestamp + canonical RunID).
60: - Follow delivers strictly increasing sequences > `--after` in batches ≤512, terminates only on terminal-lifecycle-and-drained, and treats SIGINT/SIGTERM as end-of-observation only.
61: - Cancel requests are idempotent at the store (second request returns changed=false), CAS-arbitrated against concurrent state change, and can never overwrite a won terminal.
62: - Journal content displayed was gated twice before persistence (app-layer redaction/bounding §2.8 + storage allowlist sanitize.go); text modes print no payload fields at all; support export excludes payloads and asserts exclusion of absolute workspace paths in tests.
63: - Bounded resources everywhere: list pages ≤200; event batches ≤512; export ≤1 MiB, ≤50 runs × 50 event headers, ≤100 evidence rows, ≤100 log records; local log ≤1 MiB total, ≤4 KiB/line, drop-on-overflow; payload values ≤32 KiB; encoded events ≤128 KiB; per-run journals compacted at 4096 events/16 MiB.
64: - Private-file discipline: `.ultraplan` 0700, db/log/export 0600, symlink rejection for dir/db/log, chmod verify after set (sqlite.go:154-205; local_log.go:43-65; export O_EXCL).
65: - Help paths never touch the repository or create files (test-enforced, run_commands_test.go:83-92).
66: - Stable exit-class mapping for every repository error family (mapRunControlError).
67: 
68: ## 6. Trust boundaries
69: 
70: - Operator-supplied run IDs must match the strict opaque base32 grammar before any SQL executes (id.go:73-89); cursors are decoded, size-capped, and semantically validated before use; all SQL is parameterized.
71: - Trust boundary named in the assignment: **journal payload projection passes sanitizer/redaction before display**. Runtime payloads never reach stdout verbatim: they pass the app-layer redactor/bounder (isSensitivePayloadKey, redactObservableValue, boundedPayloadValue) and then the storage allowlist gate (sanitizeEventDraft); what `follow --json` emits is the persisted, already-sanitized payload map; text modes emit only sequence/type/stage/omission-count; the support export strips payloads entirely.
72: - Sensitive-content controls operate by deny-marker matching at two layers (secret/token/password/auth*/cookie/api_key/credential…; plus prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command and absolute-path/Windows-drive rejection at storage) rather than positive encoding; `[REDACTED]` substitution applies to tool argument/result trees.
73: - Local trust model: POSIX permissions are the only access control; any local process/user that can reach `.ultraplan/` can read the store and request cancellations. No auth, session, or origin machinery exists at this door.
74: - The support export is written to an operator-chosen path with O_EXCL (refuses overwrite) and 0600; its contents include sanitized log records and classification-only reconciliation evidence.
75: - Config-sourced retention/quota values cross from yml/env into store-opening policy; source classes (default/workspace/env) are recorded into exports for provenance.
76: 
77: ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics
78: 
79: External effects per invocation: possible creation/chmod of `.ultraplan/{run-control.db,-wal,-shm,run-control.log}`; startup Reconcile writes (stalled marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals for expired/unclaimed owners past 45 s grace, reconciliation_log inserts); log appends; `cancel` appends a cancellation event and flips lifecycle to cancelling under CAS; `diagnostics --support-export` creates one new file (never overwrites); stdout/stderr/exit-code emission. Retry semantics: the observation surface itself does not retry — typed retryable flags exist on store errors (Busy/Unavailable) but only write-spine callers loop (appendRunEventWithRetry 5 s deadline, proposeRunTerminalWithRetry 250 ms windows, run_control.go:345-368). Cancellation lanes: this door only records the request; acknowledgement/delivery lives in owner control loops; a request can lose the immutable terminal race to an earlier completion (user-guide.md:384-386 documents this to operators). Restart/recovery: each fresh process re-reconciles on first command; reconcile decisions use exact process-birth identity probing and never infer success from artifact presence or PID existence alone (lifecycle.go:481-495). Error semantics: store failures classify to exit codes without leaking driver messages beyond wrapped cause text; context cancellation during store calls passes through classifyStoreError unwrapped and lands in ExitRuntime via the default arm of mapRunControlError; `follow` swallows ctx.Done as success by design.
80: 
81: ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies
82: 
83: - **run-journal-fencing** (durability-core, critical): owns the internals of the journal this surface consumes — Append fencing/CAS, sequence allocation, compaction/replay boundaries, sanitization gates, schema/migration, SQLite durability pragmas. This surface calls Repository read/cancel APIs verbatim and contributes no journal logic.
84: - **durable-operation-spine**: producer of the observed rows — controlledRuntime/durableOperationManager accept/claim/event/terminal paths (write halves live in run_control.go/durable_operations.go but belong to that surface's review scope).
85: - **cli-dispatch-exit-contract**: app.Run dispatch, global `--workspace`, exit-class constants, envelope writer, classified-error plumbing.
86: - **web-operation-hub-sse**: sibling observer; consumes `RunUseCases` and duplicates the 512/250ms/1s replay algorithm (seam `observation-replay-parity`, map.json). Web additionally returns typed `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` conflicts for out-of-window cursors (run_handlers.go:968-979); the CLI follow has no counterpart responses.
87: - **tui-console / shared-usecase-vocabulary**: consume `repositoryRunUseCases` for Runs views and dashboards.
88: - **config-inspection-health**: loadEffectiveConfig, run_control.* keys/env mapping/validation, Sources provenance map used in exports.
89: - Foundation: workspace.Discover marker walk; runcontrol retention normalization at open.
90: 
91: ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence)

97: - user-guide.md:374-391 — every runtime-backed execution receives a durable run before work starts; same ID/lifecycle/liveness/cancellation/product-status/record-state/event-cursor shown on every surface; lifecycle vs liveness vs product status are distinct axes ("running / stalled / product unknown" must not display as success); a cancellation request can lose the terminal race; closing tabs/views/quitting/interrupting follow never cancels; compacted/tombstone records stay truthful about their snapshot.
98: From ultraplan-workspace (authoritative planning context):

101: - PRD.md:162 — workspace-wide durable run list, stable inspection, replayable progress, conservative liveness, cross-surface cancellation, correlated diagnostics beginning Sprint 35.
102: - TRD.md changelog 1.7.0/1.8.0 rows (2685) — Phase 6 commitment provenance.
103: 
104: ## 10. Tests (evidence map)
105: 
106: Baseline green: internal/app 57.8% statements, internal/runcontrol 68.7% (review/baseline/go-test-cover.txt:2,12).
107:

116: runcontrol-level (store behaviors these commands project):

128: ## 11. Explicit unknowns / open questions (for later reviewers)
129: 
130: 1. Follow exposes no replay-gap signal: events below `oldest_retained_sequence` are simply absent from the stream, while TRD.md:1255 requires typed retention-gap results "rather than silently beginning a partial stream" and the web door implements `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` (run_handlers.go:968-979). 131: 2. Read commands mutate durable state via startup Reconcile (stall marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals, evidence rows). The architecture intends reconciliation-at-open, but operator-facing docs describe list/show/follow purely as inspection; the observable consequence (opening a laptop after a crash rewrites other runs' liveness/terminals as a side effect of a "read") is undocumented in-tree.

1: # Context Pack: `run-cli-observation` — Run observation and cancellation CLI
2: 
3: Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen).
4: Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
5: Domain: operator-interfaces. Risk: normal. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.
6: 
7: ## 1. Purpose
8: 
9: The `ultraplan run` subcommands are the operator's window onto the durable run-control store (`.ultraplan/run-control.db`, owned by `internal/runcontrol`). Five doors: `list` (newest-first filtered page with opaque keyset cursor), `show` (one validated snapshot), `follow` (replay committed events from a decimal sequence, then poll until the run reaches terminal state), `cancel` (reason-whitelisted durable cancellation request), and `diagnostics` (repository health projection plus an optional bounded, payload-free support export). All five are local-only: they never contact a provider (docs/cli-reference.md:492-504). The same repository capability is re-exported as `RunUseCases` for the web and TUI surfaces, making this package the shared read/cancel vocabulary for durable runs. Observation never mutates a run's lifecycle; interruption of `follow` stops observation only (run_commands.go:188-193; user-guide.md:388-391).
10: 
11: ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow
12: 
13: ### 2.1 Dispatch and repository acquisition
14: `app.Run` (app.go:88-178) dispatches `run` at app.go:161-162 to `runRun(deps, args[1:])`. `runRun` (run_commands.go:19-40) admits `--help/-h` (prints help without opening any store — test-enforced) and routes to the five handlers; unknown subcommand → ExitUsage. Every handler first calls `runRepository` (run_commands.go:42-59): workspace discovery (`--workspace` flag validated against the `ultraplan.yml` marker, else `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, else cwd upward walk; discovery.go:21-61) → ExitWorkspace class on failure; `deps.runControl == nil` → ExitRuntime "run-control.init"; `loadEffectiveConfig` → ExitConfig class; then `deps.runControl.repository(ctx, root.Path, runControlRetentionPolicy(effective.Config))` → ExitRuntime "run-control.open" on failure.
15: 
16: `runControlState.repository` (run_control.go:37-75) is a mutex-guarded per-workspace process singleton: one `*runcontrol.SQLiteRepository` plus one `LocalFileLogger`, retained for process lifetime and closed by `defer runControl.Close()` in `app.Run` (app.go:108-109). Opening performs, in order: `OpenSQLite` (creates `.ultraplan/` 0700 + `run-control.db` 0600 if absent, verifies WAL/FULL/FK/busy pragmas, migrates schema, enforces private modes; sqlite.go:60-134,154-227), logger open + `SetLogger`, then **startup `Reconcile(NativeProcessProbe{}, ReconcileOptions{})`** — so every command, including pure reads, may write (mark owners stalled, terminalize abandoned/expired-lease runs, append reconciliation_log rows). Startup reconcile failure closes both handles and aborts the command ("startup run reconciliation failed", run_control.go:66-70). A second call with a different retention policy errors deterministically ("retention policy changed during the process lifetime", run_control.go:47-49).
17: 
18: `runControlRetentionPolicy` (run_control.go:153-157) converts config strings with `time.ParseDuration`, ignoring parse errors (zero durations later fall back to defaults in `normalizeRetentionPolicy`, retention.go:13-33); quota bytes pass through.
19: 
20: ### 2.2 `run list` (run_commands.go:61-103)
21: Flags: `--json`, `--project`, `--sprint`, `--study`, `--lifecycle` (comma-separated), `--limit` (default 50; help advertises 1..200), `--after <opaque cursor>`. Help is checked before parsing; parse errors or leftover positional args → ExitUsage via `firstFlagError`. `parseLifecycleFilter` (379-392) trims/splits and validates each token against `Lifecycle.IsValid()` (11 valid states, model.go:18-41); unknown token → ExitUsage.
22: 
23: `Repository.List` (lifecycle.go:196-266): limit 0→50, bounds 1..200 else `invalidField`; filters are equality predicates on `project_id`/`sprint_id`/`study_id` plus `lifecycle IN (...)`; ordering is `updated_at DESC, run_id DESC`; `After` decodes an opaque cursor (base64url JSON `{updated_at RFC3339Nano, run_id}`, ≤1024 decoded bytes, timestamp+RunID validated; lifecycle.go:268-291) into a strict keyset predicate `(updated_at < ? OR (updated_at = ? AND run_id < ?))`; fetches limit+1 rows and, when more exist, sets `NextCursor` from the last *included* row before trimming. Each listed run is then loaded through `Snapshot` (N reads), each individually passed through `Snapshot.Validate()` (model.go:333-366). Text output prints `%s  %-20s %-18s %s` (RunID, lifecycle, liveness, slash-joined target via `formatRunTarget` 427-435), "No durable runs found." when empty, and `Next cursor: …` when paginated. JSON output uses the shared envelope (`writeJSON`, json_output.go:20-31: schema_version 1, command, workspace path, status "ok", generated_at, result = Page).
24: 
25: ### 2.3 `run show <run-id>` (105-129)
26: One positional run ID (flags reordered ahead of positionals by `orderRunArgs`, 463-481); `Snapshot(ctx, RunID(arg))` validates the opaque-ID shape first (`run_` + 26 lowercase base32 chars, id.go:65-89) → invalid shape becomes ErrInvalidArgument; missing row becomes ErrNotFound ("run is not retained"). Text rendering `renderRunSnapshot` (416-425): Run / Target / Lifecycle / Liveness / Product status (falls back to literal "unknown") / Cancellation state / Accepted / Updated (RFC3339) / Last sequence / Oldest retained sequence / History complete / Record state, plus `Terminal: outcome (reason)` when present. `--json` wraps the raw snapshot in the envelope with status "ok".
27: 
28: ### 2.4 `run follow <run-id>` (131-195)
29: Flags: `--json` (newline-delimited events), `--after <decimal sequence>` default "0" (ParseUint base 10, 64-bit; non-decimal → ExitUsage). A pre-loop `Snapshot` call validates existence before streaming. Loop body: `Events(ctx, runID, after, 512)` (sqlite.go:809-854 — strictly increasing sequences `> after`, batch cap 512, payloads decoded from stored JSON); text mode prints `seq  type(padded) stage omitted=N` (payload fields are not printed); JSON mode encodes the full persisted Event struct including its sanitized Payload map. Then a fresh `Snapshot`: loop returns nil only when `Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence`. Otherwise it waits — 250 ms after a full 512-batch or while `after < LastSequence` (catch-up), else 1 s idle — and exits cleanly on `deps.ctx.Done()` with the comment "Observation cancellation never changes the durable run". The timer starts pre-stopped (`NewTimer(0)` + drain). Polling only: the repository Notifier hook is nil in this composition.
30: 
31: ### 2.5 `run cancel <run-id>` (197-228)
32: Flags: `--json`, `--reason` default "user_requested". `canonicalCancellationReason` (394-401) whitelists exactly: `user_requested`, `operator_requested`, `shutdown_requested`, `quota_exceeded`; anything else → ExitUsage. `RequestCancellation` (lifecycle.go:70-134) trims/bounds-checks the reason, opens an immediate transaction, reloads the snapshot, and: if terminal OR cancellation state ≠ none → commits the read and returns `(current, changed=false, nil)` (idempotent no-op); otherwise appends a `cancellation` event (payload `{state: requested, reason}`) and CAS-updates `runs SET lifecycle='cancelling', cancellation_state='requested' … WHERE terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state='none' AND last_sequence = ?`; lost race → typed CodeConflict (retryable flag set). CLI text output: `Run: %s / Cancellation: %s / Changed: %t`; JSON output embeds `{changed, run: snapshot}`. Note the request is recorded regardless of owner liveness — delivery to the running owner happens owner-side (control loops acknowledge within their tick; outer-inner-double-fencing seam).
33: 
34: ### 2.6 `run diagnostics` (230-276)
35: Flags: `--json`, `--support-export <path>`. `Repository.Health` (sqlite.go:856-914) reads journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys pragmas, counts active runs (accepted/queued/running/cancelling), stalled runs (non-terminal + liveness stalled), cancellation-uncertain rows, reconciliation backlog (unclaimed past grace or expired lease past `ReconciliationGrace`=45 s, joined to attempts), oldest backlog age (min of accepted_at vs lease_expires_at over the backlog), storage bytes (all regular files prefixed `run-control.db` — db/WAL/SHM), soft/hard quotas (soft = hard − 16 MiB reserved headroom), and process-local `LocalMetrics` counters (metrics.go:17-25). Status escalates ok → degraded (≥ soft quota) → failed (≥ hard quota) with appended diagnostic strings. Text output prints nine labeled lines plus `Support export:` when written. `--json` wraps `{health, support_export?}` with the envelope **status field set to `string(health.Status)`** (ok/degraded/failed) rather than the constant "ok" used by the other four subcommands.
36: 
37: Support export (`writeRunSupportExport`, 306-377): unfiltered `List(limit 50)`; config trio (full_history, tombstone_history, workspace_quota_bytes) with source classes from `effective.Sources`; `ReconciliationEvidence(ctx, 100)` behind an anonymous-interface assertion (newest-first, evidence reduced to allowlisted classification strings, lifecycle.go:532-572); `ReadLocalLogs(root, 100)` (local_log.go:113-155 — rejects symlink/oversize/non-regular log files, skips malformed lines, keeps newest N via sliding window); per run, the first 50 events from sequence 0 reduced to `{sequence, type, omission}` — **event payloads are excluded**. The whole document is marshaled indented, rejected if > 1 MiB, then written `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY` mode 0600 (existing file → error), fsynced, closed, with deferred remove-on-failure. When `--support-export` is set, diagnostics re-runs workspace discovery and config load (251-258) even though `runRepository` already performed both.
38: 
39: ### 2.7 `RunUseCases` adapter (run_usecases.go)
40: Type aliases for all runcontrol DTOs plus sentinel error aliases (invalid-argument/not-found/conflict/unsupported-schema). `RunUseCases` (Runs/Run/RunEvents/CancelRun/RunHealth) is documented as "the surface-neutral durable observation and command boundary. Its DTOs contain only sanitized facts owned by run control"; `repositoryRunUseCases` delegates 1:1 to the Repository. Consumers: web composition (serve_commands.go:80), TUI (`useCases.runs`, tui_commands.go:51), dashboard runs page (sprint_commands.go:407). This adapter is the seam face consumed by web-operation-hub-sse and tui-console.
41: 
42: ### 2.8 Write-path context inside the assigned files (run_control.go)
43: `run_control.go` also hosts the durable write spine used by runtime-backed commands: `controlledRuntime.StartRun` (159-343) Accept→Claim→fence, persists sanitized event drafts through `OnEvent` with content-aware progress coalescing (250 ms window keyed type/stage/task/payload-hash, omission accounting merged into the next commit), a 1 s control goroutine (snapshot poll; requested cancellation ⇒ AcknowledgeCancellation + cancel; Heartbeat every 5 s under a 15 s lease; Reconcile every 10 s), persistence-failure handling that proposes `persistence_degraded` under a 30 s background context, and `terminalOutcome` mapping (deadline→timed_out, cancel→cancelled, err/failed-status→failed, else succeeded). Its sanitization pipeline feeds the journal this surface observes: `runtimeEventDraft` (417-545) maps runtime kinds to event types, drops sensitive keys (`isSensitivePayloadKey` markers secret/token/password/authorization/cookie/api_key/apikey/credential/auth), bounds keys (≤128, no control chars) and values (`boundedPayloadValue`, 32 KiB), flattens one level of nesting with a promote-list (tool/title/detail/text/delta/content/message/action/state/status/native_type/line, ≤30 entries), captures tool identity/arguments/result/error with depth-5 alias search and `redactObservableValue` string-marker redaction ([REDACTED] for Bearer [REDACTED]), and records omissions for raw-present/raw-omitted/truncated shapes. A second gate applies at storage: `sanitizeEventDraft` (sanitize.go:26-61) enforces the ~35-field allowlist (sanitize.go:10-21), adds sensitive fragments prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command (80-88), rejects absolute paths/Windows-drive strings/credential markers/control chars (90-104), replaces oversize allowed detail with a warning event, and caps encoded size at 128 KiB. The write spine itself belongs primarily to durable-operation-spine/run-journal-fencing; it is described here because the file sits inside this surface's assigned paths ... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
44: 
45: ## 3. Inputs / outputs
46: 
47: Inputs: argv (subcommand, flags, run-ID positional); workspace discovery sources (`--workspace`, `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE`, cwd marker walk); effective config incl. env overrides `ULTRAPLAN_RUN_CONTROL_FULL_HISTORY/TOMBSTONE_HISTORY/WORKSPACE_QUOTA_BYTES` (config.go:140-142) validated ≥1h/≥24h/≥64 MiB with tombstone ≥ full (config.go:487-500); `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`) and `.ultraplan/run-control.log`; wall clock; signal context (SIGINT/SIGTERM via `signal.NotifyContext`, main.go:15-17) which reaches `follow`'s wait select and repository calls as ctx cancellation.
48: 
49: Outputs: stdout human tables/lines or JSON envelopes (schema_version 1); one-line stderr errors carrying exit classes; support export file (private 0600, ≤1 MiB, O_EXCL); process exit codes from the reachable set {0, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 workspace, 5 validation/not-found, 6 runtime/store, 8 partial conflict/terminal} (app.go:15-25; mapRunControlError 403-414: ErrInvalidArgument→2, ErrNotFound→5, ErrConflict/ErrTerminal→8, everything else incl. Busy/Unavailable/Corrupt/Permission/Quota/Invariant/UnsupportedSchema→6). Side outputs common to all five doors because of pool startup: DB/WAL creation, chmod enforcement, log appends, reconcile writes (§2.1).
50: 
51: ## 4. Authoritative state
52: 
53: The authoritative durable state is entirely in `internal/runcontrol`'s SQLite store: `runs` (snapshot columns incl. lifecycle/liveness/record_state/last_sequence/oldest_retained_sequence/history_complete/omission_total/cancellation_*/terminal_*), `attempts` (fencing generations, leases, heartbeats, process birth identity), `events` (immutable — BEFORE UPDATE trigger raises; PK (run_id, sequence)), `operation_aliases`, `reconciliation_log` (evidence bounded to 16 KiB JSON, classification-only exposure on read) (schema sqlite.go:229-342). Durability posture: WAL, synchronous=FULL, foreign_keys=on, busy_timeout 5 s, immediate transactions, pragma verification at open (207-227). This surface owns no new durable state — it projects and (via cancel/reconcile) mutates through the repository. Process-local state: the `runControlState` pool (repo+logger+policy per workspace) and per-process metrics counters (not aggregate across processes). Retention/compaction (full 168h default → compacted → tombstone 720h → delete; per-run caps 4096 events / 16 MiB advancing `oldest_retained_sequence`, retention.go:58-160) reshape what observation can replay; snapshots remain truthful with explicit replay boundaries. The support export is a derived artifact, never authoritative.
54: 
55: ## 5. Invariants (as implemented)
56: 
57: - Every command, read or write, opens the same per-process repository handle and runs startup Reconcile before serving; retention policy must be stable per process (run_control.go:37-75).
58: - Every returned snapshot is validated on read (`Snapshot.Validate` enforces lifecycle/terminal/liveness coherence, timestamps monotonic from acceptance, replay-boundary arithmetic model.go:349-364); corrupt rows fail the whole command rather than render partially.
59: - List order is deterministic (updated_at DESC, run_id DESC) and pagination is keyset-based; cursors are opaque, bounded (≤1024 decoded bytes), and fully validated (timestamp + canonical RunID).
60: - Follow delivers strictly increasing sequences > `--after` in batches ≤512, terminates only on terminal-lifecycle-and-drained, and treats SIGINT/SIGTERM as end-of-observation only.
61: - Cancel requests are idempotent at the store (second request returns changed=false), CAS-arbitrated against concurrent state change, and can never overwrite a won terminal.
62: - Journal content displayed was gated twice before persistence (app-layer redaction/bounding §2.8 + storage allowlist sanitize.go); text modes print no payload fields at all; support export excludes payloads and asserts exclusion of absolute workspace paths in tests.
63: - Bounded resources everywhere: list pages ≤200; event batches ≤512; export ≤1 MiB, ≤50 runs × 50 event headers, ≤100 evidence rows, ≤100 log records; local log ≤1 MiB total, ≤4 KiB/line, drop-on-overflow; payload values ≤32 KiB; encoded events ≤128 KiB; per-run journals compacted at 4096 events/16 MiB.
64: - Private-file discipline: `.ultraplan` 0700, db/log/export 0600, symlink rejection for dir/db/log, chmod verify after set (sqlite.go:154-205; local_log.go:43-65; export O_EXCL).
65: - Help paths never touch the repository or create files (test-enforced, run_commands_test.go:83-92).
66: - Stable exit-class mapping for every repository error family (mapRunControlError).
67: 
68: ## 6. Trust boundaries
69: 
70: - Operator-supplied run IDs must match the strict opaque base32 grammar before any SQL executes (id.go:73-89); cursors are decoded, size-capped, and semantically validated before use; all SQL is parameterized.
71: - Trust boundary named in the assignment: **journal payload projection passes sanitizer/redaction before display**. Runtime payloads never reach stdout verbatim: they pass the app-layer redactor/bounder (isSensitivePayloadKey, redactObservableValue, boundedPayloadValue) and then the storage allowlist gate (sanitizeEventDraft); what `follow --json` emits is the persisted, already-sanitized payload map; text modes emit only sequence/type/stage/omission-count; the support export strips payloads entirely.
72: - Sensitive-content controls operate by deny-marker matching at two layers (secret/token/password/auth*/cookie/api_key/credential…; plus prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command and absolute-path/Windows-drive rejection at storage) rather than positive encoding; `[REDACTED]` substitution applies to tool argument/result trees.
73: - Local trust model: POSIX permissions are the only access control; any local process/user that can reach `.ultraplan/` can read the store and request cancellations. No auth, session, or origin machinery exists at this door.
74: - The support export is written to an operator-chosen path with O_EXCL (refuses overwrite) and 0600; its contents include sanitized log records and classification-only reconciliation evidence.
75: - Config-sourced retention/quota values cross from yml/env into store-opening policy; source classes (default/workspace/env) are recorded into exports for provenance.
76: 
77: ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics
78: 
79: External effects per invocation: possible creation/chmod of `.ultraplan/{run-control.db,-wal,-shm,run-control.log}`; startup Reconcile writes (stalled marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals for expired/unclaimed owners past 45 s grace, reconciliation_log inserts); log appends; `cancel` appends a cancellation event and flips lifecycle to cancelling under CAS; `diagnostics --support-export` creates one new file (never overwrites); stdout/stderr/exit-code emission. Retry semantics: the observation surface itself does not retry — typed retryable flags exist on store errors (Busy/Unavailable) but only write-spine callers loop (appendRunEventWithRetry 5 s deadline, proposeRunTerminalWithRetry 250 ms windows, run_control.go:345-368). Cancellation lanes: this door only records the request; acknowledgement/delivery lives in owner control loops; a request can lose the immutable terminal race to an earlier completion (user-guide.md:384-386 documents this to operators). Restart/recovery: each fresh process re-reconciles on first command; reconcile decisions use exact process-birth identity probing and never infer success from artifact presence or PID existence alone (lifecycle.go:481-495). Error semantics: store failures classify to exit codes without leaking driver messages beyond wrapped cause text; context cancellation during store calls passes through classifyStoreError unwrapped and lands in ExitRuntime via the default arm of mapRunControlError; `follow` swallows ctx.Done as success by design.
80: 
81: ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies
82: 
83: - **run-journal-fencing** (durability-core, critical): owns the internals of the journal this surface consumes — Append fencing/CAS, sequence allocation, compaction/replay boundaries, sanitization gates, schema/migration, SQLite durability pragmas. This surface calls Repository read/cancel APIs verbatim and contributes no journal logic.
84: - **durable-operation-spine**: producer of the observed rows — controlledRuntime/durableOperationManager accept/claim/event/terminal paths (write halves live in run_control.go/durable_operations.go but belong to that surface's review scope).
85: - **cli-dispatch-exit-contract**: app.Run dispatch, global `--workspace`, exit-class constants, envelope writer, classified-error plumbing.
86: - **web-operation-hub-sse**: sibling observer; consumes `RunUseCases` and duplicates the 512/250ms/1s replay algorithm (seam `observation-replay-parity`, map.json). Web additionally returns typed `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` conflicts for out-of-window cursors (run_handlers.go:968-979); the CLI follow has no counterpart responses.
87: - **tui-console / shared-usecase-vocabulary**: consume `repositoryRunUseCases` for Runs views and dashboards.
88: - **config-inspection-health**: loadEffectiveConfig, run_control.* keys/env mapping/validation, Sources provenance map used in exports.
89: - Foundation: workspace.Discover marker walk; runcontrol retention normalization at open.
90: 
91: ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence)
92: 
93: From ultraplan-go docs (in-tree):
94: - cli-reference.md:492-520 — durable run command grammar; all commands workspace-scoped, provider-free; list newest-first default 50, opaque cursor, "active means only accepted/queued/running/cancelling"; follow replays committed events, polls quickly while catching up and ≤1 Hz idle; interrupting follow stops observation only; cancellation idempotent and never overwrites an already-terminal winner; diagnostics reports schema/WAL, quota, retention, active/stalled ownership, backlog; `--support-export` creates a private bounded ≤1 MiB file containing safe snapshots, event headers/omission facts, health, config source classes, reconciliation decisions, newest sanitized `.ultraplan/run-control.log` records, excluding payloads/prompts/provider data/source content/credentials/arbitrary output/absolute workspace path.
95: - cli-reference.md:474-491 — the compatibility-sensitive stable JSON list does **not** include the run subcommand envelopes (config/health/study/code/sprint only).
96: - cli-reference.md:18-30 — numeric exit-class table (0..8).
97: - user-guide.md:374-391 — every runtime-backed execution receives a durable run before work starts; same ID/lifecycle/liveness/cancellation/product-status/record-state/event-cursor shown on every surface; lifecycle vs liveness vs product status are distinct axes ("running / stalled / product unknown" must not display as success); a cancellation request can lose the terminal race; closing tabs/views/quitting/interrupting follow never cancels; compacted/tombstone records stay truthful about their snapshot.
98: From ultraplan-workspace (authoritative planning context):
99: - TRD.md:2184-2225 (§18C Phase 6) — durable envelope contents; acceptance atomic before child start; redact-before-persist; monotonic per-run sequences committed before fan-out; compaction retains explicit snapshot + lower replay boundary so clients distinguish complete replay from gap; workspace-wide active queries; cancellation idempotent, durably recorded, arbitrated single winner; conservative liveness (PID insufficient); lease+fencing; recorded reconciliation evidence exposing stalled/interrupted/cleanup_uncertain; required cross-process matrix includes cursor expiry and a redacted support bundle.
100: - TRD.md:1254-1255 — Sprint 35 event records monotonic, sanitized, durable-before-live-fanout; replay via explicit cursor where duplicate delivery is safe and unavailable cursors produce a typed retention-gap result "rather than silently beginning a partial stream".
101: - PRD.md:162 — workspace-wide durable run list, stable inspection, replayable progress, conservative liveness, cross-surface cancellation, correlated diagnostics beginning Sprint 35.
102: - TRD.md changelog 1.7.0/1.8.0 rows (2685) — Phase 6 commitment provenance.

106: Baseline green: internal/app 57.8% statements, internal/runcontrol 68.7% (review/baseline/go-test-cover.txt:2,12).

128: ## 11. Explicit unknowns / open questions (for later reviewers)
129: 
130: 1. Follow exposes no replay-gap signal: events below `oldest_retained_sequence` are simply absent from the stream, while TRD.md:1255 requires typed retention-gap results "rather than silently beginning a partial stream" and the web door implements `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` (run_handlers.go:968-979). Whether the CLI's silent-empty behavior satisfies the contract for operators is unresolved in-tree; likewise `--after` beyond `LastSequence` on a non-terminal run polls at 1 Hz indefinitely without feedback.
131: 2. Read commands mutate durable state via startup Reconcile (stall marks, interrupted/cleanup_uncertain terminals, evidence rows). The architecture intends reconciliation-at-open, but operator-facing docs describe list/show/follow purely as inspection; the observable consequence (opening a laptop after a crash rewrites other runs' liveness/terminals as a side effect of a "read") is undocumented in-tree.
132: 3. 306: func writeRunSupportExport(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, workspaceRoot string, health runcontrol.Health, effective config.Effective, path string) error {
307: 	page, err := repository.List(ctx, runcontrol.Query{Limit: 50})
308: 	if err != nil {
309: 		return err
310: 	}
311: 	export := runSupportExport{
312: 		SchemaVersion: 1,
313: 		Health:        health,
314: 		Config: runSupportConfig{
315: 			FullHistory: effective.Config.RunControl.FullHistory, FullHistorySource: effective.Sources["run_control.full_history"],
316: 			TombstoneHistory: effective.Config.RunControl.TombstoneHistory, TombstoneSource: effective.Sources["run_control.tombstone_history"],
317: 			WorkspaceQuota: effective.Config.RunControl.WorkspaceQuota, WorkspaceQuotaFrom: effective.Sources["run_control.workspace_quota_bytes"],
318: 		},
319: 		Runs: page.Runs,
320: 	}
321: 	if reader, ok := repository.(interface {
322: 		ReconciliationEvidence(context.Context, int) ([]runcontrol.ReconciliationEvidence, error)
323: 	}); ok {
324: 		export.Reconciliation, err = reader.ReconciliationEvidence(ctx, 100)
325: 		if err != nil {
326: 			return err
327: 		}
328: 	}
329: 	export.Logs, err = runcontrol.ReadLocalLogs(workspaceRoot, 100)
330: 	if err != nil {
331: 		return err
332: 	}
333: 	for _, snapshot := range page.Runs {
334: 		events, err := repository.Events(ctx, snapshot.RunID, 0, 50)
335: 		if err != nil {
336: 			return err
337: 		}
338: 		item := runSupportEvents{RunID: snapshot.RunID}
339: 		for _, event := range events {
340: 			item.Events = append(item.Events, struct {
341: 				Sequence uint64               `json:"sequence"`
342: 				Type     runcontrol.EventType `json:"type"`
343: 				Omission *runcontrol.Omission `json:"omission,omitempty"`
344: 			}{event.Sequence, event.Type, event.Omission})
345: 		}
346: 		export.Events = append(export.Events, item)
347: 	}
348: 	encoded, err := json.MarshalIndent(export, "", "  ")
349: 	if err != nil {
350: 		return err
351: 	}
352: 	if len(encoded) > 1<<20 {
353: 		return errors.New("support export exceeds 1 MiB limit")
354: 	}
355: 	file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
356: 	if err != nil {
357: 		return err
358: 	}
359: 	ok := false
360: 	defer func() {
361: 		_ = file.Close()
362: 		if !ok {
363: 			_ = os.Remove(path)
364: 		}
365: 	}()
366: 	if _, err := file.Write(append(encoded, '\n')); err != nil {
367: 		return err
368: 	}
369: 	if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
370: 		return err
371: 	}
372: 	if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
373: 		return err
374: 	}
375: 	ok = true
376: 	return nil

Then in loop, Reset(wait) and select on idle.C or ctx.Done. On each iteration, timer already fired and been drained? After select receives from idle.C, next iteration calls Reset(wait) — since channel drained, Reset works correctly. If ctx.Done wins the select, we return nil. OK.

TRD:1255 requires typed retention-gap result rather than silent partial stream. The web door implements cursor_ahead/replay_gap; CLI doesn't. The context pack flags this as an open question. Is this a defect within my review lens ("bugs the current verification would allow", verification/operability)? The CLI follow with `--after 0` on a compacted run will silently stream partial history while claiming "History complete" maybe false in snapshot. Actually snapshot has HistoryComplete field shown in `show`. For follow text mode there's no indication of gap. This is a real operability/verification concern backed by TRD CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence (TRD.md:1254-1255). Severity moderate, confidence depends on whether TRD applies to CLI. Let me check web's implementation to confirm parity divergence.

4. **Envelope status divergence** for diagnostics --json (status = health.Status). Contract says stable JSON envelope has status "ok"; but run JSON surfaces are excluded from the compatibility-sensitive list. Probably non-issue / minor.

5. **`writeRunSupportExport` uses unfiltered List(limit 50)** — newest 50 runs only; silent truncation. Contract says bounded ≤50 runs — documented bound. Non-issue.

6. **Support export size check**: `len(encoded) > 1<<20` before appending newline; writes encoded+newline ≤ 1MiB+1. Immaterial.

7. **O_EXCL failure removes existing file?** No—OpenFile fails, return err before defer set up. Good. But note: on write error path, deferred remove deletes the partially written file. Good.

8. **`runCancel` output**: text prints `Cancellation: %s` with snapshot.Cancellation.State. After successful request, state is "requested". Idempotent second call prints changed=false with current state. Fine.

9. **mapRunControlError**: ErrInvalidArgument → ExitUsage (2). Hmm, exit code table says 2 usage, 5 validation/not-found, 8 conflict/terminal. InvalidArgument mapping to usage seems intentional. But note `run cancel --reason bogus` → ExitUsage before repository open — good (no DB side effects).

10. **Startup Reconcile on reads**: mutating durable state during inspection commands — flagged as unknown #2. Architecture intends reconcile-at-open. Not a defect per doctrine (FUTURE-INTENT vs CURRENT-CONTRACT?). Docs describe list/show/follow as pure observation ("interrupting follow stops observation only"), and cli-reference says commands are provider-free reads. The observable consequence: `ultraplan run list` after crash rewrites other runs' terminals. Is this contrary to any current contract? user-guide says closing tabs never cancels — reconcile terminalizing abandoned runs isn't cancellation by operator. It's intended architecture (TRD requires reconciliation). I'd call this a defended non-issue unless docs promise read-only. Let me check docs quickly.

11. **`parseLifecycleFilter`**: splits on ","; empty token between commas → part "" → IsValid() false → ExitUsage "unknown lifecycle \"\"". Reasonable.

12. **`firstFlagError(err, fs.Args())`**: When parse succeeds but NArg>0, reports unexpected argument. Fine.

13. **`run list` help check placement**: `helpRequested(args)` scans all args including positionals; `run list somefile --help` prints help instead of usage error. Minor.

14. **Potential real bug — `run list --limit 0`**: passes Limit=0 to store; store clamps 0→50. But help says 1..200. So operator typing `--limit 0` gets 50 results, silently. Store treats 0 as default. Out-of-range like 201 → invalidField error → ErrInvalidArgument → ExitUsage. Minor inconsistency, documented bounds violated silently for 0 only. Low severity.

15. **Negative limit**: `fs.Int` accepts `--limit=-5` → store bounds 1..200 → invalid → ExitUsage. fine.

16. **`runDiagnostics` double discovery/config**: benign duplicate work; also inconsistency risk minimal. Non-issue.

17. **`writeRunSupportExport` anonymous interface assertion**: if repository is a different impl (tests?), reconciliation section omitted silently — support export missing evidence without notice. In production composition always SQLiteRepository. Non-issue.

18. **Health.Metrics process-local counters** presented as workspace-wide facts in diagnostics/export — could mislead operators (unknown #10). Observability gap, low severity.

19. **`runFollow` JSON encoder error handling**: returns raw err (not classified). Write errors to stdout (EPIPE etc.) → app.Run wraps? Let me check how app.Run handles returned errors — probably prints to stderr with class. A broken-pipe mid-follow yields runtime-classified error message. Cosmetic.

20. **Events batch cap**: `repository.Events(ctx, runID, after, 512)` hard-coded 512 matches contract ≤512.

21. **`runFollow` busy-loop hazard**: if `after >= snapshot.LastSequence` and lifecycle not terminal, wait = 1s (since len(events)==0 and after >= LastSequence) → fine. If `after > LastSequence` (operator passed future sequence), same 1 s poll forever until terminal. Documented? Unknown #1 mentions indefinite polling without feedback. Operability nit.

22. **Snapshot validation failing whole command** — corrupt row kills entire listing; acceptable design.

23. **`renderRunSnapshot` ProductStatus fallback "unknown"** — firstSafeValue(ProductStatus,"unknown"). OK.

24. **Cancellation reason whitelist mismatch with store**: RequestCancellation trims/bounds-checks reason; whitelist is CLI-side. Are there reasons accepted elsewhere (e.g., internal shutdown_requested?) consistent? Check runcontrol model for canonical reasons. If the web/TUI accept additional reasons (e.g., "superseded"), asymmetry minor.

25. **`runControlRetentionPolicy` swallows ParseDuration errors**: config.Load validates ≥1h etc.? Context says config.go:487-500 validates. But env overrides ULTRAPLAN_RUN_CONTROL_FULL_HISTORY validated too? Need to check: if env override is malformed, does loadEffectiveConfig reject or silently ignore? If silently ignored → zero duration → normalizeRetentionPolicy defaults apply → retention policy differs from what operator configured, silently. That's an error-truth finding if config validation skips env overrides. Let me check config.go:140-142 and 487-500.

26. **Retention policy stability check**: compares struct equality; policies map keyed by root. Two commands in one process with same config → same policy. Fine.

27. **`runRepository` opens pool + startup Reconcile even for reads — performance hazard**: every read pays migration+reconcile cost. Intended architecture. Non-issue per doctrine.

28. **`runFollow` initial Snapshot validates existence but its LastSequence isn't used to seed anything** — fine.

29. **JSON follow emits full persisted Event including Payload map** — payload was sanitized at two layers. Trust boundary holds. But wait — does storage sanitize guarantee no absolute paths? sanitize rejects absolute path strings in allowed fields. Payload keys allowlisted. OK.

30. **Support export includes LocalLogRecord contents** — ReadLocalLogs redacts? local_log.go claims redacting logger. Test asserts export excludes absolute workspace root. OK.

31. **`run diagnostics` text output prints `Oldest backlog age: %s`** — duration string; fine.

32. **Exit code for `run follow` interrupted by SIGINT**: returns nil → exit 0. Contract-conformant.

33. **A subtle one — `runFollow`'s select drains ctx.Done but continues looping if neither fires; on ctx.Done during Events()/Snapshot() calls (not in select), mapRunControlError maps context.Canceled → default arm → ExitRuntime error printed.** So Ctrl+C during an active store call (e.g., slow disk, busy timeout 5s) produces an ugly "runtime" error and exit code 6 instead of clean exit 0. Signal arrives → signal.NotifyContext cancels ctx → in-flight SQLite call returns context.Canceled error → classifyStoreError unwrapped → mapRunControlError default → ExitRuntime "run.follow: ... context canceled". The comment says observation cancellation never changes durable run — true, but the UX/error-truth is wrong-ish: interrupting follow usually exits 0 cleanly (select branch), but racy window exits 6 with error text. Also worse: after SIGINT during the *initial* Snapshot (line 152), same. This is a genuine error-truth/operability finding: interrupt classification inconsistent. Severity low-medium. Confidence: need to verify classifyStoreError passes context.Canceled unwrapped and no retry. Let me check sqlite.go classifyStoreError.

34. **`runCancel` when run already terminal**: RequestCancellation returns (current, false, nil) — prints Changed:false, Cancellation:none, exit 0. Contract: idempotent. But should exiting 0 be right when cancellation lost terminal race? user-guide documents loss. Exit 0 with Changed:false communicates. OK.

36. **`Query.Limit` bounds enforced in store; CLI default 50.**

37. **`orderRunArgs` bug candidate**: `name := strings.SplitN(arg, "=", 2)[0]`; for valued flag with `=` form (`--reason=shutdown_requested`), isFlag true, appended whole; good. For `--after` followed by another flag (`--after --json`): i+1 consumed blindly → flags=["--after","--json"], positionals=[id]. Then Parse: --after gets "--json" value?? No wait — flags slice order preserved: ["--after","--json"] then positionals. stdlib Parse sees `--after` needs value → takes "--json" as its value!     Real problem: `run follow <id> --after` (missing value at end): i+1 out of range → flags=["--after"], Parse errors "flag needs an argument" → ExitUsage. fine.

38. **`helpRequested` before parse means `run cancel <id> --help` prints help and exits 0 without opening repo — consistent with help contract.**

39. **Potential defect: `run list` JSON envelope `result` is Page struct — does Page include Runs nil vs []?** Empty page JSON `"runs": null` maybe. Consumers might break; cosmetic.

40. **`writeRunSupportExport` writes file even if `path` points inside .ultraplan or anywhere; O_EXCL prevents clobber. Path traversal irrelevant (operator-chosen).**

41. **Export includes full Snapshots (page.Runs) — do snapshots contain sensitive target fields? Targets are metadata strings boundedSafe'd. OK.**

42. **Health escalation thresholds**: soft quota = hard − 16MiB; if hard quota < 16 MiB, soft negative? Config validates ≥64 MiB. OK.

146: 		return "", classifyStoreError("stat_workspace", "workspace root cannot be inspected", err)
147: 	}
148: 	if !info.IsDir() {
149: 		return "", invalidField("workspace_root", "must be a directory")
150: 	}
151: 	return filepath.Clean(root), nil
152: }

154: func preparePrivateDatabase(root string) (string, error) {
155: 	directory := filepath.Join(root, ".ultraplan")
156: 	info, err := os.Lstat(directory)
157: 	switch {
158: 	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
159: 		if err := os.Mkdir(directory, 0o700); err != nil {
160: 			return "", classifyStoreError("create_directory", "create private run-control directory failed", err)
161: 		}
162: 	case err != nil:
163: 		return "", classifyStoreError("inspect_directory", "inspect run-control directory failed", err)
164: 	case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir():
165: 		return "", invalidField("run_control_directory", "must be a real directory, not a symlink")
166: 	}
167: 	if err := enforcePrivateMode(directory, 0o700); err != nil {
168: 		return "", err
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	path := filepath.Join(directory, "run-control.db")
172: 	info, err = os.Lstat(path)
173: 	switch {
174: 	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
175: 		file, createErr := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
176: 		if createErr != nil {
177: 			return "", classifyStoreError("create_database", "create private run-control database failed", createErr)
178: 		}
179: 		if closeErr := file.Close(); closeErr != nil {
180: 			return "", classifyStoreError("close_database", "close new run-control database failed", closeErr)
181: 		}
182: 	case err != nil:
183: 		return "", classifyStoreError("inspect_database", "inspect run-control database failed", err)
184: 	case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.Mode().IsRegular():
185: 		return "", invalidField("run_control_database", "must be a regular file, not a symlink")
186: 	}
187: 	if err := enforcePrivateMode(path, 0o600); err != nil {
188: 		return "", err
189: 	}
190: 	return path, nil
191: }

193: func enforcePrivateMode(path string, want fs.FileMode) error {
194: 	if err := os.Chmod(path, want); err != nil {
195: 		return classifyStoreError("set_permissions", "set private run-control permissions failed", err)
196: 	}
197: 	info, err := os.Stat(path)
198: 	if err != nil {
199: 		return classifyStoreError("verify_permissions", "verify run-control permissions failed", err)
200: 	}
201: 	if got := info.Mode().Perm(); got != want {
202: 		return wrapError(CodePermission, "verify_permissions", fmt.Sprintf("private permissions are %04o; require %04o", got, want), false, nil)
203: 	}
204: 	return nil
205: }

207: func verifyPragmas(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) error {
208: 	checks := []struct {
209: 		name string
210: 		want string
211: 	}{
212: 		{name: "journal_mode", want: "wal"},
213: 		{name: "synchronous", want: "2"},
214: 		{name: "foreign_keys", want: "1"},
215: 		{name: "busy_timeout", want: "5000"},
216: 	}
217: 	for _, check := range checks {
218: 		var got string
219: 		if err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "PRAGMA "+check.name).Scan(&got); err != nil {
220: 			return classifyStoreError("verify_pragma", "verify required SQLite durability policy failed", err)
221: 		}
222: 		if !strings.EqualFold(got, check.want) {
223: 			return wrapError(CodeInvariant, "verify_pragma", fmt.Sprintf("SQLite %s=%s; require %s", check.name, got, check.want), false, nil)
224: 		}
225: 	}
226: 	return nil
227: }
