C confirmed at code level: context.Canceled inside a store call → classedError class=6 (ExitRuntime), message "run.follow: context canceled". So SIGINT landing inside Events/Snapshot/Reconcile produces exit 6 + runtime-error stderr, while the same SIGINT landing in the timer select exits 0 silently. Nondeterministic outcome of identical operator action.

Now let me also verify the diagnostics text-mode observability claim (Diagnostics strings + storage/quota numbers not printed in text mode) — that's plain from code lines 269-274: prints Status but not health.Diagnostics nor StorageBytes/SoftQuotaBytes/HardQuotaBytes. Let me double check there's no other printing... Confirmed from read: only nine labeled fields + Support export line. And JSON includes them via struct marshal. So text-mode operator seeing "Status: degraded" gets no reason. Also worth checking: does anything print Health.Diagnostics elsewhere? rg.

Also double-check one more candidate before writing up: the envelope status divergence — non-issue. The support export truncation silence + newest-50-only runs — low. Health.Metrics process-local zeros — low. Let me quickly sanity-check whether diagnostics degraded status is even reachable/tested: quota escalation requires storage ≥ soft quota = hard − 16 MiB. Reachable with big DB. Not tested per context pack. Fine as part of finding D (text mode hides escalation cause).

One more thing to check: `run list --limit 0`. Store treats 0 → default 50. Help says 1..200. Minor validation-truth gap. I'll fold into minor/non-issues.

Also check ReadLocalLogs symlink/oversize handling briefly to defend trust boundary claims — context says tested. Skip deep dive; owned by local log tests.

Also confirm no test covers follow gap/cursor-ahead (context pack says so; my grep of app tests confirms none).

Let me also quickly verify the "cancel on already-terminal run exits 0" behavior matches docs — yes idempotent.

One more potential issue to examine: `writeRunSupportExport` calls `repository.Events(ctx, snapshot.RunID, 0, 50)` per run — for tombstone runs events may be few; fine. Export includes Runs snapshots with Correlation (product_run_id etc.) — safe identifiers.

And the anonymous-interface assertion for ReconciliationEvidence — production repo is *SQLiteRepository which implements it; fine.

Now, is there anything about **follow not using the repository Notifier** — polling only, documented ("polls ... at most once per second"). Fine.

**List N+1**: each Snapshot separately validated; a single corrupt row fails entire page — design choice ("corrupt rows fail the whole command rather than render partially" per invariant). Fine.

Now severity/confidence calibration:

Finding 1 (silent partial replay / no retention-gap signal in CLI follow):
- Claim: CLI `run follow` begins a partial stream silently when requested cursor is below oldest retained sequence, and polls forever without feedback when cursor is ahead of LastSequence on a non-terminal run.
- Bad outcome: operator/script believes replay is complete history (exit 0, uninterrupted stream); debugging/audit conclusions drawn from missing events; indefinite silent hang for bad cursors.
- Trigger: any compacted run (per-run cap 4096 events / 16 MiB — reachable in normal long sprints; verified at 2300 events × 8 KB payloads) or any --after > LastSequence.
- Evidence: run_commands.go:161-194 (no boundary checks); lifecycle.go compaction sets oldest_retained/history_complete=0; web counterpart run_handlers.go:968-980 implements cursor_ahead/replay_gap; TRD.md §12.3 line ~1255 & §18C line ~2197; empirical repro.
- Controls/counter-evidence: snapshot exposes HistoryComplete/OldestRetainedSequence via `run show`; user-guide says compacted records remain truthful about snapshot; cli-reference wording "replays committed events" is weaker than TRD. But TRD is authoritative planning contract and explicitly forbids silent partial stream; parity seam exists.
- Severity: medium (operator-facing correctness/observability; no data loss or security). Confidence: high.

Finding 2 (interrupt classification nondeterminism):
- Ctrl+C during in-flight store call → exit 6 + "run.follow: context canceled" (classifiedCause ExitRuntime), vs exit 0 clean when in select. Also affects initial Snapshot/startup Reconcile windows. Scripts treating nonzero as failure misread intentional interrupts; error truth wrong ("provider.runtime" code for an operator interrupt).
- Severity: low. Confidence: high mechanism (code-verified), medium impact.

I'll note it as minor observation attached to export discussion, maybe fold into non-issues with caveat. I'll list under minor/low findings? Keep as defended-with-caveat non-issue to avoid noise. Hmm. The doctrine says report substantive only. # Findings — `config-inspection-health`

## F1. Workspace YAML parser silently discards unmatched list items (fail-open admission)
- **Claim**: In `loadFile`, a `- item` line is routed through `switch listField` (internal/platform/config/config.go:225-244) which has **no default case**; whenever no list header is active (`listField == ""`) or the field isn't one of the five known lists, the line is silently dropped.
- **Bad outcome**: A workspace config line vanishes with zero diagnostics and loading succeeds. Reproduced: `models:\n  - workspace/default` → `err=nil`, `models.default="provider/model"` (placeholder), `source="default"`. Runs then execute against a placeholder provider/model and fail far from the misconfiguration site. Same silent swallow for an item appended after a scalar inside a section (`smoke:\n  run_timeout: 10m\n  - oops`).
- **Trigger**: Any mistyped list under a scalar key, item before its header, or column-0 list header (config.go:213 requires leading whitespace > 0 to recognize a nested list header; otherwise the header itself becomes a bogus *section* and its items are dropped).
- **Evidence**: config.go:225-245 (switch without default → `continue`); contrast scalar unknowns which fail closed ("unknown config field", config.go:420), as promised by docs/configuration.md ("Unsupported fields are rejected"). No test covers stray items.
- **Counter-evidence searched**: downstream `Validate` does not catch it because defaults fill every required field — the run proceeds "healthy".
- **Severity**: Medium. **Confidence**: High (reproduced).
- **Regression test**: `Load` with `models:\n  - x` must return an error naming the offending line; item-under-scalar and column-0-header cases included.

## F2. Clearing a list via empty header leaves provenance claiming `"default"`
- **Claim**: An empty list header (`required_health:` with no items) calls `clearListField` (config.go:216, 255-258) which resets the default-populated slice to nil, but never sets `Sources[field] = "workspace"` (only per-item appends do, lines 230-241).
- **Bad outcome**: Reproduced: `agentwrap.required_health:` (empty) → value `[]` (vs. 3-item default), `Sources["agentwrap.required_health"]=="default"`. Same for `smoke.environment`. `config show --json` — a stable, script-consumed surface whose stated purpose is source metadata (docs/configuration.md:14) — reports the wrong origin for a value that differs from default.
- **Trigger**: Any empty list header in `ultraplan.yml`.
- **Evidence**: config.go:211-223 (clear path sets no source), 227-243 (source set only on items).
- **Severity**: Low-Medium (misleads exactly the debugging flow provenance exists for). **Confidence**: High (reproduced).
- **Regression test**: after loading a config with an emptied list, assert `Sources[field] == "workspace"`.

## F3. Emptying `agentwrap.required_health` silently flips health to the strictest possible gate
- **Claim**: `Validate` accepts an empty list (config.go:517-521 iterates nothing). `RequestFromConfig` copies nil (internal/platform/runtime/runtime.go:551); `Adapter.Health` sends empty `Checks`/`RequiredChecks` (internal/platform/runtime/health.go:47,51,55-62); agentwrap's OpenCode adapter then expands empty `Checks` to **all eight** default checks including `provider`/`authentication`/`model` probes (agentwrap/opencode/health.go:47-59), and `RequiredHealthFailure` with empty `required` treats *every result* as required (`explicitRequired=false` path, agentwrap/health.go:121-131).
- **Bad outcome**: An operator who empties the list to relax runtime gates gets the opposite: probes like `opencode providers list provider` run against the placeholder split of `models.primary="provider/model"` (runtime.go:542, `splitModel`) and fail on any real machine → `health` exits 6. Provenance simultaneously claims "default" (F2), so the change looks self-inflicted-by-defaults.

# Findings — `config-inspection-health`

## F1. Workspace YAML parser silently discards unmatched list items (fail-open admission)
- **Claim**: In `loadFile`, a `- item` line is routed through `switch listField` (internal/platform/config/config.go:225-244) which has **no default case**; whenever no list header is active (`listField == ""`) or the field isn't one of the five known lists, the line is silently dropped.
- **Bad outcome**: A workspace config line vanishes with zero diagnostics and loading succeeds. Reproduced: `models:\n  - workspace/default` → `err=nil`, `models.default="provider/model"` (placeholder), `source="default"`. Runs then execute against a placeholder provider/model and fail far from the misconfiguration site. Same silent swallow for an item appended after a scalar inside a section (`smoke:\n  run_timeout: 10m\n  - oops`).
- **Trigger**: Any mistyped list under a scalar key, item before its header, or column-0 list header (config.go:213 requires leading whitespace > 0 to recognize a nested list header; otherwise the header itself becomes a bogus *section* and its items are dropped).
- **Evidence**: config.go:225-245 (switch without default → `continue`); contrast scalar unknowns which fail closed ("unknown config field", config.go:420), as promised by docs/configuration.md ("Unsupported fields are rejected"). No test covers stray items.
- **Counter-evidence searched**: downstream `Validate` does not catch it because defaults fill every required field — the run proceeds "healthy".
- **Severity**: Medium. **Confidence**: High (reproduced).
- **Regression test**: `Load` with `models:\n  - x` must return an error naming the offending line; item-under-scalar and column-0-header cases included.

## F2. Clearing a list via empty header leaves provenance claiming `"default"`
- **Claim**: An empty list header (`required_health:` with no items) calls `clearListField` (config.go:216, 255-258) which resets the default-populated slice to nil, but never sets `Sources[field] = "workspace"` (only per-item appends do, lines 230-241).
- **Bad outcome**: Reproduced: `agentwrap.required_health:` (empty) → value `[]` (vs. 3-item default), `Sources["agentwrap.required_health"]=="default"`. Same for `smoke.environment`. `config show --json` — a stable, script-consumed surface whose stated purpose is source metadata (docs/configuration.md:14) — reports the wrong origin for a value that differs from default.
- **Trigger**: Any empty list header in `ultraplan.yml`.
- **Evidence**: config.go:211-223 (clear path sets no source), 227-243 (source set only on items).
- **Severity**: Low-Medium (misleads exactly the debugging flow provenance exists for). **Confidence**: High (reproduced).
- **Regression test**: after loading a config with an emptied list, assert `Sources[field] == "workspace"`.

## F3. Emptying `agentwrap.required_health` silently flips health to the strictest possible gate
- **Claim**: `Validate` accepts an empty list (config.go:517-521 iterates nothing). `RequestFromConfig` copies nil (internal/platform/runtime/runtime.go:551); `Adapter.Health` sends empty `Checks`/`RequiredChecks` (internal/platform/runtime/health.go:47,51,55-62); agentwrap's OpenCode adapter then expands empty `Checks` to **all eight** default checks including `provider`/`authentication`/`model` probes (agentwrap/opencode/health.go:47-59), and `RequiredHealthFailure` with empty `required` treats *every result* as required (`explicitRequired=false` path, agentwrap/health.go:121-131).
- **Bad outcome**: An operator who empties the list to relax runtime gates gets the opposite: probes like `opencode providers list provider` run against the placeholder split of `models.primary="provider/model"` (runtime.go:542, `splitModel`) and fail on any real machine → `health` exits 6. Provenance simultaneously claims "default" (F2), so the change looks self-inflicted-by-defaults.
- **Trigger**: `required_health:` emptied in workspace YAML; docs document no empty-list semantics (docs/configuration.md only shows populated lists; Validation section doesn't reject it).
- **Counter-evidence searched**: scaffold always populates the list (internal/workspace/init.go:171-175); no consumer treats empty as "skip runtime checks"; behavior is stricter, not weaker, so no security hole — but it is undocumented, unvalidated semantics inversion.
- **Severity**: Medium-Low. **Confidence**: High on mechanics (code-traced end-to-end), Medium on intent.
- **Regression test**: `Validate` should reject an explicitly emptied `required_health` (or the empty form must be defined and documented); assert either way.

## F4. Redaction skips `agentwrap.extra_args`
- **Claim**: `redactAgentwrap` redacts only `Executable` and `Env` (internal/platform/config/redaction.go:72-78); `ExtraArgs` passes through raw into `Redacted` and is printed verbatim by the stable `config show --json` surface (internal/app/config_commands.go:41-43).
- **Bad outcome**: Reproduced: `ExtraArgs=["--api-key=sk-live-abc123", "--provider-header=Bearer ghp_xyz"]` survive `Redact` unchanged while the equivalent `Env` item becomes `[REDACTED]`. `Sensitive()` already carries arg-form markers precisely shaped for this (`"--key"`, `" key="`, redaction.go:30) — they are just never applied to the one field whose contents are CLI arguments passed to the runtime subprocess (opencode.go:34-39).
- **Trigger**: Secret-bearing extra arg in `ultraplan.yml`; visible to anyone reading terminal scrollback/CI logs of `config show --json`.
- **Counter-evidence**: docs advise against tokens in YAML (configuration.md:234) and text-mode `config show` omits extra_args entirely — leak is `--json`-only. Still contradicts "redacts sensitive-looking values in config … output" for a defense the same file implements for sibling free-form fields.
- **Severity**: Low-Medium. **Confidence**: High (reproduced).
- **Regression test**: `Redact` must apply `RedactValue("agentwrap.extra_args", ...)` per item; assert `--api-key=…` → `[REDACTED]`.

## F5. Version metadata cannot be stamped; `version` always reports placeholders
- **Claim**: `Version` values come from package consts (internal/app/version.go:5-9) wired only via `app.DefaultVersion()` in main (cmd/ultraplan/main.go:20). There are no package-level `var`s for `-ldflags -X`, CI builds plain `go build` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:27), and the release checklist's cross-compile commands have no ldflags either (docs/release-checklist.md:53-56).
- **Bad outcome**: Verified by building and running: `Version: 0.0.0-local / Commit: local / BuildDate: local` for any build, including releases. The checklist acceptance item "`ultraplan version` reports intended build metadata" (release-checklist.md:151) is unmeasurable as wired, and support/diagnostics cannot identify a deployed binary — an operability gap on one of this surface's three entrypoints.
- **Severity**: Low. **Confidence**: High.
- **Regression/fix verification**: convert consts to vars, stamp via ldflags in CI/release scripts, add a test asserting non-placeholder output when `Config.Version` is injected.

## F6. Health probes have no deadline anywhere (`Timeout` is a dead parameter)
- **Claim**: `HealthRequest.Timeout` (internal/platform/runtime/health.go:14) is never read; `Adapter.Health` never sets `agentwrap.HealthCheckRequest.Timeout` (health.go:55-62; agentwrap applies it only if >0, opencode/health.go:18-22); `runRuntimeHealth` passes the caller's context, which in production is the bare signal context (cmd/ultraplan/main.go:15-17).
- **Bad outcome**: Every probe shells out to `opencode` sequentially (up to 8 checks given F3's expansion). One wedged subcommand hangs `ultraplan health` indefinitely — a command docs position for scripted use (cli-reference.md:74 "script-friendly"), where no human Ctrl-C exists.
- **Counter-evidence searched**: probes get no stdin and bounded output capture, but nothing bounds wall-clock; no timeout is imposed by `runHealth` either.
- **Severity**: Low-Medium (operability). **Confidence**: High on dead parameter/facts, Medium on real-world hang frequency.
- **Regression test**: fake `HealthChecker`/process runner that blocks; assert health returns within a configured deadline with a classified failure.

## F7. Verification gap: the health aggregation layer has zero direct coverage
- **Claim**: All four app-level health tests stub `runtimeHealthChecks` (internal/app/health_commands_test.go:104-111), and `fakeRuntime` in the runtime package implements only `StartRun`/`Capabilities`, so `NewAdapter` leaves `health=nil` and `Adapter.Health` is never executed by any test; `runRuntimeHealth`'s report→check mapping is equally unexercised.
- **Bad outcome**: The code that decides capability gates and status mapping (runtime/health.go:43-103) — logic that feeds exit codes and the stable `health --json` envelope — can regress silently. I exercised it myself with a fake `HealthChecker`: capability-downgrade (`sessions` unsupported → error + status `unsupported`) and degraded-required-failure both behave correctly, so this is unprotected rather than currently-broken; F1-F3 each also lack a failing-test witness, which is how they survived.
- **Severity**: Low-Medium (per review lens: fake-only confidence). **Confidence**: High (verified by exhaustive grep plus filling the gap with scratch tests).

## Defended non-issues (counter-evidence found)
- **Capability-probe swallow branch** (`if caps, err := a.Capabilities(ctx); err == nil`, runtime/health.go:74) looks fail-open but is unreachable for OpenCode: `Capabilities()` returns a static table and never an error (agentwrap/opencode/options.go:132-157).
- **Warn-status check with exit 0** is impossible: `Checks == RequiredChecks` and `RequiredHealthFailure` fails required checks on degraded/unknown/unsupported/transient (agentwrap/health.go:138-156).
- **Exit precedence** config(3) > runtime(6) > structure(5) matches implementation; `validation.Issues[0]` is safe (issues non-empty iff invalid, workspace/validation.go:28).
- **Unbounded upper side of `execution.default_parallel`/`default_retries`** matches the current documented validation contract (configuration.md "Validation" enumerates exactly what is rejected); consumers enforce ≥1 (study_commands.go:327). Watch item, not a defect.
- **Parser edges fail closed**: CRLF, BOM, single quotes, inline comments, oversized lines (>64KiB scanner limit), unreadable `ultraplan.yml`, empty scalars for required fields — all produce load/validation errors. (`filesystem.read: ok` asserts existence, not readability, but a subsequent unreadable file correctly fails `config.validation`.)
- **QA lower-only bounds, malformed-env attribution, precedence, double redaction, env summary counting**: implemented as specified and genuinely tested (config_test.go covers max/zero/negative per field and failed overrides don't claim env source).context-run-cli-observation

# Findings — `run-cli-observation` (verification/operability lens)

## F1. CLI `follow` silently begins a partial stream after compaction and polls forever on ahead-of-journal cursors — no retention-gap or cursor-ahead signal
- **Claim**: The follow loop (internal/app/run_commands.go:161-194) never compares the requested `--after`, nor the first fetched sequence, against `snapshot.OldestRetainedSequence` or `LastSequence`. It prints whatever `Events(after, 512)` returns and exits 0 when terminal-and-drained.
- **Bad outcome** (both reproduced):
  1. *Silent partial replay*: seeded a non-terminal run, appended 2300 progress events x8 KB until per-run compaction fired (`record_state=compacted`, `oldest_retained_sequence=257`, `history_complete=false`). `ultraplan run follow <id> --after 0 --json` printed its first event at **sequence 257**, streamed silently to ctx-cancel, exit 0, stderr empty. Sequences 1-256 are gone from the output with zero indication. An operator auditing a long sprint sees an exit-0 stream and reasonably treats it as complete history.
  2. *Indefinite silent wait*: `follow <id> --after 999999` on a running run: full observation window produced **zero output**, no error, exit 0 on interrupt. The operator cannot distinguish "caught up, waiting" from "cursor points past everything ever committed".
- **Contract**: TRD §12.3 (projects/ultraplan-go/docs/TRD.md ~:1255): "an unavailable cursor produces a typed retention-gap result plus the current durable run snapshot rather than silently beginning a partial stream". TRD §18C (~:2197): the store retains the lower replay boundary "so clients can distinguish complete replay from a gap"; the required cross-process matrix explicitly includes cursor expiry. The web door implements exactly this (internal/web/run_handlers.go:968-980: typed `cursor_ahead` and `replay_gap` conflicts); the CLI has no counterpart. The seam map (`observation-replay-parity`) records the divergence and no test pins CLI behavior — this is a contract bug the current verification allows.
- **Existing controls / counter-evidence searched**: `run show` does print `History complete: false` and `Oldest retained sequence`, but nothing links it to follow output; cli-reference's weaker phrasing ("follow replays committed events") does not override the authoritative TRD; compaction is routine, not exotic (per-run caps 4096 events / 16 MiB, retention.go:58-95 — reached here at ~18 MB of journal).
- **Severity**: Medium (operator-facing correctness of the primary observation tool; no data loss/security impact). **Confidence**: High (reproduced end-to-end).
- **Regression test**: app-level test seeding a compacted non-terminal run must fail today: assert follow emits a typed gap/cursor-ahead signal (or refuses) for `--after` below oldest-retained and for `--after` > LastSequence, instead of a silent exit-0 stream/poll.

## F2. Interrupting `follow` nondeterministically exits 6 with a runtime-error message when the signal lands inside a store call
- **Claim**: SIGINT received while blocked in the timer select exits 0 ("Observation cancellation never changes the durable run", run_commands.go:188-193). But SIGINT landing inside `repository.Events`/`Snapshot`/startup `Reconcile` returns raw `context.Canceled` — `classifyStoreError` passes context errors through unwrapped (sqlite.go:1103-1105) — which `mapRunControlError`'s default arm classifies as ExitRuntime (run_commands.go:411-413), so `fail()` prints `run.follow: context canceled` and exits 6.
- **Verified**: scratch assertion: `mapRunControlError("run.follow", context.Canceled)` → class=6, code=`provider.runtime`, message=`"run.follow: context canceled"`.
- **Bad outcome**: the identical operator action produces exit 0 or exit 6 depending on sub-millisecond timing. Scripts that treat nonzero as failure misread an intentional interrupt as a runtime fault; the error truth is wrong (`provider.runtime` for operator cancellation). The dirty window dominates during large catch-up replay (time spent in Events/Snapshot, not select) and during startup reconcile contending up to busy_timeout=5s.
- **Counter-evidence searched**: docs promise only that interrupting "stops observation only" (user-guide.md:388-391) — durably true; they do not promise a clean exit code, so this is an internal consistency/error-truth defect rather than a documented-contract breach.
- **Severity**: Low. **Confidence**: High on mechanism (code + unit verified), Medium on real-world frequency.
- **Regression test**: drive follow with a context cancelled while a slow/stubbed Events call is in flight; assert exit 0 and empty stderr (fix: check `deps.ctx.Err()` before mapping store errors in the loop).

## F3. Text-mode diagnostics prints escalated Status with no reason and no quota numbers
- **Claim**: Health escalates ok→degraded/failed solely on storage vs soft/hard quota and appends explanatory strings ("soft quota reached; new run acceptance is paused", sqlite.go:906-912). The text renderer (run_commands.go:269-274) prints nine fixed lines that exclude both `health.Diagnostics` and `StorageBytes`/`SoftQuotaBytes`/`HardQuotaBytes`; those fields reach humans only via `--json`.
- **Bad outcome**: `ultraplan run diagnostics` reports `Status: degraded` (or `failed`) with zero explanation of why, while cli-reference.md:516 promises diagnostics "reports schema/WAL, quota, ...". Acceptance is being paused workspace-wide and the human-readable door says nothing about the cause or thresholds.
- **Verification gap**: no test exercises degraded/failed status or text-mode diagnostics end-to-end (confirmed by reading run_commands_test.go and agreeing with the context pack's coverage notes).
- **Severity**: Low-Medium (observability). **Confidence**: High.
- **Regression test**: produce storage ≥ soft quota (or inject Health) and assert text output contains the diagnostic string and quota bytes when status != ok.

## F4. Support export/diagnostics JSON present process-local metrics as unqualified workspace facts — always near-zero from the CLI process
- **Claim**: `Health.Metrics = r.metrics.snapshot()` (sqlite.go:858) counts only operations performed by *this* process (metrics.go). A `run diagnostics [--support-export]` process performs no Accept/Append/Terminal, so the exported `"metrics"` object always shows acceptance/append/terminal counts ≈0 regardless of workspace activity; it is embedded bare into the support bundle and JSON envelope.
- **Bad outcome**: a support engineer reading the export concludes no events were appended / no runs accepted — misleading precisely in the diagnostic flow the export exists for. The process-local qualifier lives only on the Go type comment (metrics.go:11), never in the artifact.
- **Counter-evidence searched**: counters are accurate for the serving web/TUI process; no consumer annotates provenance. Facts certain; harm requires a misreading, but the artifact invites it.
- **Severity**: Low. **Confidence**: High on facts, Medium on harm.
- **Fix/regression**: either drop Metrics from the CLI projection/export or label them (e.g. `metrics_scope: "process"`); regression asserts the qualifier.

## Defended non-issues (counter-evidence found)
- **Read commands mutate state via startup Reconcile** (stall marks, interrupted terminals): intended architecture per TRD §18C reconciliation-at-open with recorded evidence; user-guide's "interrupting never cancels" remains true (reconcile outcomes are owner-loss arbitration, not operator cancellation). Docs could be clearer; not a defect.
- **`runControlRetentionPolicy` swallows `time.ParseDuration` errors** (run_control.go:154-156): unreachable in composition — `config.Load` validates durations ≥1h/≥24h and quota ≥64 MiB before repository open (config.go:175, 487-500), failing ExitConfig. Dead defensiveness.
- **Envelope status divergence** (`diagnostics --json` uses health.Status vs constant "ok"): deliberate escalation signal; run envelopes are excluded from the compatibility-sensitive stable-JSON list (cli-reference.md:474-491). Non-issue.
- **Cancel semantics**: idempotent read-commit return on terminal/existing request (lifecycle.go:91-96), CAS single-winner, immutable terminal protected; reason whitelist enforced CLI-side before any store open so bad reasons cause zero DB side effects; matches documented idempotency and terminal-race loss.
- **Trust boundary holds**: `follow --json` emits only twice-gated persisted payloads (app-layer redaction/bounding in runtimeEventDraft + storage allowlist sanitizeEventDraft); text modes print sequence/type/stage/omission-count only; support export strips payloads entirely (verified struct) and its test asserts exclusion of seeded event content and the absolute workspace root.
- **List N+1 Snapshot loads / mixed vintages**: bounded ≤200 rows, each validated; staleness window benign for a listing; corrupt row fails the whole page by stated invariant. Cost linear but bounded.
- **`orderRunArgs` edges** (`--reason --json id`, unknown flags, `=` forms): worst cases yield usage-class errors; no wrong-success path found.
- **Follow timer discipline** (`NewTimer(0)`/Stop/drain/Reset): traced all branches — no busy loop, no missed fire; empirically paced as documented (250 ms catch-up / 1 s idle). Terminal runs always retain their final terminal event, so drain termination is reachable even for tombstones.
- **Export file discipline**: O_EXCL|0600, fsync, remove-on-failure, size guard (pre-newline measurement is immaterial, ≤1 MiB+1); existing-file collision fails without truncation.
- Minor watch items below reporting threshold: `--limit 0` silently yields default 50 despite advertised 1..200 bounds (store clamps 0→50, lifecycle.go:198-200); text omission lines drop the omission Reason (JSON carries it); support-export truncation (newest-50 runs, first-50 events/run) carries no marker.

- **F1 (Medium, high confidence, reproduced)** — CLI `follow` has no retention-gap or cursor-ahead signal (run_commands.go:161-194). On a compacted non-terminal run, `--after 0` silently began replay at sequence **257 of 2300**, streamed to exit 0 with no marker; `--after 999999` polled forever with zero output. TRD §12.3 forbids "silently beginning a partial stream" and the web door implements typed `cursor_ahead`/`replay_gap` (run_handlers.go:968-980) — the CLI diverges from both contract and sibling surface, and no test pins it.
- **F2 (Low, mechanism verified)** — Ctrl+C landing inside an Events/Snapshot/reconcile store call classifies as ExitRuntime (`run.follow: context canceled`, exit 6) while the same interrupt in the timer select exits 0 — nondeterministic outcome for an intentional observation-only interrupt.
- **F3 (Low-Medium)** — text-mode diagnostics prints escalated `Status: degraded/failed` without `health.Diagnostics` or storage/quota bytes; the escalation cause is JSON-only.
- **F4 (Low)** — support export embeds process-local metrics that are structurally ≈0 for any fresh CLI process, unqualified, inviting "nothing was appended" misreads.

Defended non-issues include read-triggered reconcile (intended per TRD §18C), the ParseDuration swallow (unreachable — config.Load validates first), envelope status divergence, cancel idempotency/CAS, the two-layer payload trust boundary, list N+1 boundedness, and follow timer discipline.
